A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 46-page versions of the same BAH dataset paper. Text and rendered-page comparisons cover the main text, figures, tables and Appendices A–I without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v5 reports original dataset analyses and experiments on BAH, including frame/video classification, zero-shot recognition and personalized domain adaptation in Section 3 and Appendix I.

after.justification: v7 retains these original empirical results, including classification benchmarks, prompt/context experiments and domain-adaptation measurements in Section 3 and Appendix I.

M1.justification: The annotation pipeline, model architectures, temporal/fusion components, zero-shot inference and domain-adaptation procedures are unchanged. No method component is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same BAH data from 300 Canadian participants and 1,427 videos for frame/video classification, zero-shot recognition and personalization. Pretraining dataset coverage is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the corresponding experiments, including LFAN/CAN/MT/JMT fusion in Tables 6 and 19, Video-FocalNet variants in Table 17, and Source-only/MMD/Sub-Based/SHOT/NRC/Oracle in Table 24.

E3.justification: The 195/30/75 participant split, preprocessing, AVGF1/AP metrics, training budgets, model configurations and testing procedures are identical. Appendix I retains the same video aggregation, zero-shot windows and personalization protocols.

E4.justification: The modality/fusion, visual-input, context-window and prompt analyses are unchanged, as are demographic and annotator-cue analyses. Section 3 and Appendices E–I contain no added or removed analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report five repetitions with different seeds and mean/standard deviation in Table 15, and mean/standard deviation across target participants in Table 24. Annotation-agreement reporting is also unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted findings and result entries are unchanged. For example, CAN retains AVGF1 0.5526/AP 0.2631 in Table 6, and Sub-Based retains AVGF1 0.5417/AP 0.3739 in Table 24.

T1.justification: Neither version contains a theorem/proof contribution. Existing metric definitions and mathematical expressions are unchanged, with no added formal assumptions, derivations or corrections.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about the novel BAH dataset, preliminary benchmarks and need for specialized temporal and multimodal modeling.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning context, modality conflicts and personalization are unchanged. Section 4 recommendations and Appendix B limitations concerning recording quality, participant representation and frame imbalance are retained verbatim.

D1.justification: The repository address and embedded links change from github.com/sbelharbi/bah-dataset to github.com/LIVIAETS/bah-dataset in the abstract, Section 2.3 and Figure 11. This updates access information; implementation details, hardware, licensing and dataset-request procedures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Reference 43 gains CVPR 2025 workshop venue information and revised bibliographic formatting, but still identifies the same 8th ABAW work.

P1.justification: Small editorial changes affect author-list punctuation, the arXiv version/date stamp and reference 43's initials, capitalization and publication details. Scientific prose and the organization of the main text and appendices are unchanged.

P2.justification: The author line has small spacing changes, and the expanded reference 43 causes local bibliography reflow on page 44. Figure 11 updates its repository text. Figure/table structures, captions, plots and placements otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v7 supplies a different repository address and fuller venue information for reference 43, with small typographic changes. The complete empirical evidence, methods, claims and limitations remain intact. These limited maintenance edits do not amount to a meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
